messages:
sara: Ran a canary matrix toggling per-layer quant (fp8/int8/4-bit) with embeddings + lm_head excluded. Seeing a ~12% p95 latency uplift on Dedicated pool and periodic CPU spikes. Posting quick logs and config we used.

miguel: Which pool/hardware and batcher settings?

sara: Dedicated - rtx-a100-pool-1. Batcher: max_batch_ms=6, max_tokens=2048, hysteresis_ms=3. KV warmup enabled. See config snippet: 
```yaml
quant_map: per_layer
exclude_layers: [embedding, lm_head]
quant_modes: [fp8, int8, int4]
batcher:
  max_batch_ms: 6
  hysteresis_ms: 3
kv:
  warmup: true
  eviction_policy: lru
kernel_selector:
  sticky_steps: 0
```

anya: Hm, hysteresis_ms=3 is pretty low. Small batches + kernel dispatch cost for mixed precision can kill p95. Did you capture kernel switch counts?

sara: Yep — perf counters show frequent kernel switches and memcpy spikes when the per-layer toggles are active. Snippet from the profiler: 
```
[profiler] timeline: conv_kern_fp8 run_count=214 memcpy_s2d=1.2MB/s
[profiler] timeline: attention_int8 run_count=198 memcpy_s2d=3.9MB/s
[kernel_selector] switches_last_min=92 sticky_hits=6
[kv] cache_miss_rate=0.087 evictions=123
latency: baseline_p95=72ms canary_p95=80.6ms
```

devon: That kernel_selector switches_last_min=92 is suspicious. If kernels keep flipping between fp8 and int8 we pay dispatch + reconfigure cost. Try kernel sticky of 20 steps to bias toward last used kernel for each micro-batch.

rahul: Also check KV compatibility: partial quant often leads to variant kernels with different KV layout expectations. If the runtime falls back or rebuilds KV buffers it'll thrash. Are we reserializing KV to fp32 on mismatch?

sara: Looking at logs, we see "kv_layout_mismatch -> rebuild_kv_buffer" 30x in one minute. So yes, there is rebuild churn.

miguel: Two parallel mitigations to try: 1) enforce kernel stickiness to reduce switches, 2) ensure a compatibility shim so all quant variants share a canonical KV layout (or pin layers that touch KV to a single precision). Also try increasing hysteresis_ms to 12 to build larger batches.

anya: Agreed. Also run the same canary with embedding+lm_head excluded vs embedding+lhead pinned to fp32 to see delta. Excluding can avoid accuracy regressions but might still cause layout churn if mid layers change types.

sara: I'll schedule a matrix: variables = [quant_modes: {fp8,int8,int4}, kernel_sticky: {0,20}, hysteresis_ms: {3,12}, kv_compat: {shim,on}] across 3 seed prompts. Job id: 12345. deploy-bot: kicked off the job.

deploy-bot: Canary job 12345 started on rtx-a100-pool-1. ETA ~5h. Logs: https://ci.internal/jobs/12345

devon: One more thought — for partial quant we might implement a safety gate: if p95 regresses >5% or kv_rebuild_rate > 0.02 within first N minutes, auto-fallback to mixed-precision baseline. Saves manual rollbacks.

rahul: We should also add a lightweight per-request tag so the profiler can correlate kernel switches with specific prompt patterns (long prefix vs short prompt). Sometimes prefix-heavy requests force large KV interactions.

sara: Good call. I'll add request_tagging to the job and export CSV of kernel events + kv ops. Will report back with the 24h matrix results.

miguel: Thanks — once you have the CSV ping me. If kernel stickiness + kv shim recovers p95 we can make that default for per-layer toggles.

sara: noted. If it still regresses I'll try pinning entire attention blocks to a single quant mode (safety mask) and re-run.

anya: Nice. Short-term: increase hysteresis, enable kernel_sticky=20, and test kv_compat=shim. That should give us a clear signal.

sara: on it. Running the first 3 configs now, will update the thread with a concise table when done. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
